notes:
Meeting notes / call snippets:
- Jan 28 demo (hosted API): good initial latency (mean gen latency ~120ms token-level in region us-east-1) — product team impressed with streaming and function-calling.
- POC executed Feb 03-17: 2-week POC using hosted API with production-like traffic (50 rps peak, 15k tokens/session typical). Results: prefix caching reduced token cost ~18%.
- Team preference: start hosted API for quick launch -> move to Dedicated for cost predictability and VPC isolation Q3.
- Pricing focus in procurement: commit baseline, burst capacity, overage pricing, ramp schedule and early-termination protection.
- Quote from VP Eng (R. Patel): "Need a guarantee on peak handling and an explicit overage cap — we can't get surprised at EOM."
- Security: require SSO/SAML (Okta), SOC2, audit logs to integrate with internal SIEM, key material in customer KMS. Data residency: primary US but want EU-satellite for EU customers later.
- Legal asked for residency addendum + model fallback SLA (if Dedicated pool unavailable fallback to Redwood-hosted with defined latency delta).
- Commercials: asked for 12m and 24m commit options, monthly ramp schedule and ability to buy burst credits at a predictable uplift. Also asked whether unused commit rolls forward (no currently).
- Procurement quibble: want initial ramp (month 1 = 25% commit, month 2 = 50%, month 3 = 75%) and 6-month acceleration clause tied to usage growth.
- Internal stakeholders: VP Eng (R. Patel), Head of Product (J. Morales), Procurement lead (A. Chen). AE -> Maya Singh. SE -> Liam Carter. CSM -> tentative (Elena Morales).
- Action items: draft Dedicated pricing addendum with explicit commit, burst, overage caps; sample invoice schedule; SSO integration plan; security questionnaire follow-up (drive link).

poc_summary: Hosted API POC ran with a synthetic workload mirroring prod: 50 rps peaks, avg session 15k tokens. Observed mean token gen latency ~120ms in us-east-1; KV/prefix caching reduced token spend ~18%. No functional regressions. SE validated fallback path to a smaller model with 2x latency but acceptable UX for non-interactive paths.
pricing_terms_discussed: Option A: 12-month commit = baseline 500M tokens/month; burst pool: +30% burst at 1.5x unit rate; overage = 1.8x unit rate capped at 40% of monthly invoice
Option B: 24-month commit = baseline 300M tokens/month; lower unit price, burst +50% at 1.3x rate; overage = 1.6x unit rate with 30% cap
Ramp schedule requested by customer: M1=25% baseline, M2=50%, M3=75%, M4+ = 100%
Burst credits: prepaid add-on or on-demand (customer prefers predictable prepaid burst blocks)
Service credits / fallback SLA: automatic route to Redwood-hosted fallback if Dedicated pool unavailable >5m, with 60% credit pro-rata (legal flagged exact wording)
